- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior day’s high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show price > forecast, adjust downward by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in early periods (e.g., 1–5 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 1–3% to early forecast points.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from midpoint of sentiment transition window.
